fields.text: **How do I register a module?**: Call `app.registerModule(&myModule);` inside `setup()`. The framework uses compile-time type introspection to auto-register it. See `references/registration.md` for rules and lifecycle details.
**What include do I use?**: Always use `#include "AppFoundation.h"`. Do not couple directly to internal framework header paths.

**How does firmware talk to the LVGL display?**: Via `sys_*` reactive subjects (never direct widget manipulation). The framework updates subjects using `lv_subject_set_int()` and `lv_subject_copy_string()`, and LVGL observers (`bind_text`, `bind_value`, `LV_USE_OBSERVER`) update the bound UI widgets automatically.

**How does a consumer extend the UI?**: Fork the `uidesign/` project folder into the application repository, preserve all 23 contracted `sys_*` subjects so framework screens and modals continue functioning, and add custom `app_*` subjects with corresponding widgets and screens. Export the design to the `UIDesign` PlatformIO library.

**What is the `sys_` prefix?**: `sys_` denotes framework-contracted reactive subjects (e.g. `sys_boot_progress`, `sys_error_visible`, `sys_ota_status`). Designers must not rename or remove these subjects in their LVGL Pro projects so core framework events (boot splash, OTA updates, WiFi configuration, error states, diagnostics) bind correctly.
**How much DRAM does BLE cost?**: ~69 KB on ESP32-S3 (controller ~35-40 KB non-negotiable + host ~25-30 KB tunable). See `docs/developer/bluetooth.md` § Memory & DRAM Budget.
**Can BLE buffers use PSRAM?**: No. BLE controller DMA cannot access PSRAM. `MEM_ALLOC_MODE_EXTERNAL` causes spinlock panics (IDFGH-7560). All BLE memory must be internal DRAM.
**How do I add a GATT service?**: Implement `IBLEServiceProvider`, register in `main.cpp` via `bleManager.registerServiceProvider()`. See `docs/developer/bluetooth.md` § Peripheral Role.
**How do I connect to a remote BLE device?**: Implement `IBLEClientProvider`, register via `bleManager.registerClientProvider()`. See `docs/developer/bluetooth.md` § Central Role.
**How do I reduce BLE memory usage?**: Choose a memory profile from the BLE Memory Profiles section below. The `peripheral-only` profile saves ~15-20 KB by dropping Central/Observer roles.
**What is `bleInUse()`?**: A strong symbol override in `BLEStack.cpp` that prevents Arduino's `initArduino()` from releasing BT controller memory. Without it, BLE init crashes with WDT resets.

**What BLE services does the framework provide?**: The framework automatically registers a standard Bluetooth SIG Device Information Service (DIS, UUID `0x180A`) in `BLEManager::begin()`. It exposes 6 read-only characteristics: Manufacturer (`app.getManufacturer()`, defaults to `"CB Labs"`), Model (`app.getAppName()`), Serial Number (last 3 bytes of WiFi MAC), Firmware Revision (`BUILD_VERSION`...

**What TX power does BLE use?**: +20 dBm (maximum). Set in two places that must agree: `NimBLEDevice::setPower(20, NimBLETxPowerType::All)` in `BLEStack::init()`, and `CONFIG_BT_CTRL_DFT_TX_POWER_LEVEL_P20=y` in `sdkconfig.ble.defaults`. The `setPower()` call sets ADV, SCAN, and DEFAULT power types. It does NOT affect WiFi TX power.

**What is the BLE advertising interval?**: 50ms (80 × 0.625ms units). Set in `BLEStack::startAdvertising()` via `setMinInterval(80)` / `setMaxInterval(80)`. This is twice as fast as Apple's recommended ≤100ms for quick discovery.

**Should I call `esp_coex_preference_set()`?**: **No.** Leave it at the ESP-IDF default (`PREFER_WIFI`, enum 0). `PREFER_BT` starves WiFi entirely (portal unreachable). `PREFER_BALANCE` causes `AUTH_EXPIRE` during WiFi 802.11 association. WiFi auth frames have a 1-second deadline and need priority. BLE stability comes from +20 dBm TX power and deferred connection parameters instead. See `docs/d...

**Why doesn't the framework call `updateConnParams()` on connect?**: Apple and Android guidelines mandate waiting ≥5 seconds after connection before requesting L2CAP parameter updates. Calling `updateConnParams()` immediately on `PeerConnected` collides with the central's MTU exchange and GATT service discovery, causing Android (nRF Connect) to drop with GATT CONN TIMEOUT (Error 147/0x93 + Er...

**What is the WiFi STA connection timeout?**: 15 seconds per attempt, with indefinite STA-first retries using exponential backoff (5 s / 10 s / 30 s / 60 s). After 3 minutes of continuous STA downtime, a fallback AP starts in `WIFI_AP_STA` mode (portal reachable while STA keeps retrying). The fallback AP is torn down when STA reconnects. WiFi never falls back to AP-only mode when credentials ar...

**How do WiFi and BLE coexist?**: `CONFIG_ESP_COEX_SW_COEXIST_ENABLE=y` in sdkconfig enables hardware-level RF time-sharing. The framework adds five application-level mechanisms: Running-Only gating, ScanInhibit tokens, Administrative Pause, Duty Cycle Clamping, and Exponential Backoff. See `docs/developer/bluetooth.md` § Coexistence & Radio Hardening.

**States**: `Unknown` (0), `Healthy` (1), `Degraded` (2), `Quarantined` (3), `Suspended` (4).
**Exponential Backoff**: 30s base delay (`HEALTH_BACKOFF_BASE_MS`), doubling up to a 15-minute cap (`HEALTH_BACKOFF_CAP_MS`).
**Quarantined**: Reached 15m ceiling. Continues probing every 15 minutes to automatically self-heal if the remote service recovers.
**Suspended**: Hard failure (`AuthError`). Retries cease to preserve radio and API rate limits. Exited via `DataManager::resetSourceHealth()` or an explicit `requestPriorityFetch()`.

**Portal**: Data Sources card on Status tab with live state badges and reset action.
**Display**: Deferred vector+mutex subscriber in `U8G2DisplayModule` and `LVGLDisplayModule`.
**MCP Server**: `get_data_sources` built-in tool returns current health snapshots and backoff timings.

T2 has **no root `src/main.cpp`**, meaning the framework cannot be compiled standalone from root. The entry point exists only in `template/src/main.cpp`. This fundamentally changes the project topology from a buildable library+app to a library-only layout. The spec explicitly requires a root entry point per the Hollywood Principle.

T2's S3 partition table declares SubType `spiffs` but the codebase uses `LittleFS` — this will cause a filesystem mount failure on the S3 target. T2's 17 explicit `-I` flags in `platformio.ini` is also a maintenance hazard; adding a new module requires updating 3 environment sections.

T1 has **3.75× more test code** than T2 and covers **100% of modules** vs T2's **42%**. T2's gap is particularly concerning for safety-critical modules like `WifiManager`, `OtaUpdateManager`, and `DataManager` — all untested.

**Deterministic Lifecycle & Boot Gating**: A structured 3-state application lifecycle (`Booting` → `Configuring` ↔ `Running`) governed by **`PreconditionEngine`**, which evaluates system prerequisites, gates normal execution, continuously monitors runtime health, and attributes failures with Cause and Severity to prevent wedged device states.

**Hardened Web Administration**: High-performance PROGMEM Single Page Application (SPA) served by `PsychicHttpServer`, backed by **`AuthManager`** for robust portal authentication, secure session cookies, JWT bearer tokens, and captive portal provisioning.

**Observability & Secret Scrubbing**: Structured **`LogPipeline`** coupled with **`Redactor`** (`ISanitizer`) for real-time in-flight scrubbing of Wi-Fi credentials, API keys, and sensitive tokens before writing to serial or remote log ring buffers.

**Tamper-Evident Audit Trail**: **`AuditModule`** recording critical system events, boot transitions, auth attempts, and configuration mutations into a compact, flash-wear-mitigated, tamper-evident log (`BOARD_AUDIT_BYTES`).

**Extensible Module Model**: Defined extension points (`IConfigurable`, `ITickable`, `IDataSource`, `IWebContributor`, `IMCPContributor`, `IPreconditionContributor`) allowing domain modules to self-register via `registerModule()` without touching the kernel.
**Zero Kernel Changes**: Adding, configuring, or removing optional modules requires only changes to `platformio.ini` and app setup code via the module registration bus.

**Lightweight arrays** (`KeyManager` entries, web routes, config consumers) — `std::vector` that may grow at any time since additions do not affect loop scheduling or carousel timing. No `shrink_to_fit()` required.

**`getConfigNamespace()`**: Returns a unique compile-time string literal (e.g. `"wifi"`, `"display"`, `"ota"`). Determines file location at `/mod/<namespace>.json`.
**`getSchemaVersion()`**: Returns the integer schema version (starting at 1). Incremented when configuration key structures change.
**`applyConfig(const JsonObject& section)`**: Deserializes configuration into internal state during boot (`beginAll()`) or portal configuration imports. The JSON object is guaranteed to be complete.
**`serializeConfig(JsonObject& section)`**: Serializes current configuration state into the JSON object. `ConfigManager` injects the metadata field `_v` automatically.

**`migrateConfig(JsonObject& section, int fromVersion)`**: Invoked when stored `_v` is older than `getSchemaVersion()`. Modules modify the JSON object in-place (renaming keys, adding new defaults). Returning `true` persists the migrated format; `false` falls back to defaults.
**`resetConfig()`**: Resets all module settings to hardcoded factory defaults. Called before factory resets or when configuration files are missing or corrupt.

**`UpdateStatus`**: Enum indicating fetch result: `Success` (0), `NoChange` (1, HTTP 304), `RateLimited` (2, HTTP 429), `FetchError` (3, network/TLS/timeout), `ParseError` (4, malformed payload), `AuthError` (5, 401/403 or missing credentials), `Skipped` (6, source declined to fetch due to missing prerequisites).
**`PriorityTier`**: Scheduling cadence: `High` (0, ~60s), `Normal` (1, ~300s / 5 min), `Low` (2, ~1800s / 30 min).

**Phase 1 — Registration Window:** During `setup()`, modules are pushed into vectors via `app.registerModule()`. Vectors may reallocate and temporarily fragment the heap — this is acceptable because it occurs before long-lived runtime objects are created.

**Phase 2 — Compact and Lock:** Inside `app.begin()`, the framework calls `_compactAndLock()`. This method iterates through every internal vector, calls `shrink_to_fit()` to release unused capacity back to the heap, and sets `_locked = true`.

**Phase 3 — Runtime Rejection:** Any attempt to call `app.registerModule()` after `app.begin()` has been invoked will instantly trigger a **fatal panic**. Late registration is forbidden because pushing to a locked vector could cause a heap reallocation during steady-state execution.

**Late registration causes a fatal panic.** All modules MUST be registered in `setup()` before calling `app.begin()`. If a module should be conditionally inactive, register it unconditionally and have its `tick()` return early based on internal state.
**No Runtime Cost**: Stubs are compile-time only. Production builds link directly against the true ESP-IDF or Arduino headers.
**No Inline Guards**: Production code remains clean and free of `#ifdef` preprocessor directives.

**API Mirroring**: Stub headers (`test/stubs/platform/`) mirror the exact API surface of ESP-IDF and Arduino functions. During native test builds (`env:native`), the include path priority ensures the compiler resolves `#include <esp_system.h>` to the stub implementation.

**`Priority::Required`**: Guaranteed placement in primary advertising. If the primary payload exceeds 31 bytes, a `BLE Advertising` precondition fault is raised.

**Main Loop Execution**: All provider callbacks (`onPeerConnected`, `onPeerDisconnected`, `onSubscriptionChanged`, `onConnected`, `onNotification`, `onDisconnected`, `onDevicePaired`, `onDeviceForgotten`) run strictly on the **main application loop** during `Application::tick()`.
**No Mutexes Required**: Because callbacks execute in the main loop thread, provider implementations do not need mutexes or thread synchronization against NimBLE tasks.

**Dedicated Background Worker**: Asynchronous operations that require blocking I/O (initiating central connections, GATT service discovery, pairing negotiation) run on a dedicated worker task (`centralWorkerTask`, 4KB stack, priority 3).

**Queue Protection**: If the FreeRTOS event queue between the host task and main loop fills up under extreme event bursts, dropped events increment a diagnostic counter exposed in `/api/ble/status` and on the web portal.

**Timer staggering is NOT a coexistence mechanism.** Coexistence is dynamic hardware-level RF arbitration managed by the ESP32 MAC/PHY layer (`CONFIG_ESP_COEX_SW_COEXIST_ENABLE`). Staggering application timers only smooths FreeRTOS queue contention; it does not arbitrate radio packet collisions.

**Single Include:** Use `#include "AppFoundation.h"` instead of including individual interface headers. `AppFoundation.h` transitively includes all interfaces, `FrameworkConfig`, and the `Application` hub.

**Forward Declarations:** Use forward declarations (e.g. `class PsychicHttpServer;`) in your header file instead of full `#include` statements to reduce compile times and prevent circular dependency loops.
**Interfaces Inheritance:** Standard multiple inheritance is used to implement multiple interfaces.
**`override` Keyword:** Always mark inherited virtual functions with `override` to allow the compiler to detect signature mismatches.

**10ms Execution Budget:** Your `tick()` implementation MUST execute quickly and return in **10 milliseconds or less** as per the `ITickable` contract. If your module performs blocking operations (like raw socket reads, heavy math, or slow sensor queries), defer them to a FreeRTOS task or use the asynchronous background `DataManager` via `IDataSource`.

**Unified Composition Model:** Both custom application modules (like `MyApp`) and framework optional modules (like `HomeAssistantModule` or `LVGLDisplayModule`) follow the exact same wiring pattern: they are instantiated at file/static scope in `main.cpp` and passed to `app.registerModule()`. See [Using Optional Modules](using-optional-modules.md) for details on feature-flagged optional modules.
**Never Use `delay()`:** Using `delay()` blocks the entire thread, halting WiFi operations, display rendering, web services, and other modules. Use the `currentMillis` comparison pattern instead.

**Avoid Runtime Heap Allocation:** Avoid using `new`, `std::vector::push_back`, or Arduino `String` manipulation inside `tick()`. Allocate all memory upfront during initialization or on the stack to prevent heap fragmentation.
**Implement `#ifdef ESP_PLATFORM` Guards:** Ensure your module compiles on host CPUs by mocking out target-specific hardware headers (e.g. wire drivers, ESP32 specific registers).
**Adhere to the 10ms Budget:** Profile your `tick()` callback to ensure it returns within 10ms.
**Namespace Configs:** Keep your configuration keys short and group them under a unique, lowercase namespace (e.g., `wifi`, `clock`, `myapp`).
**Follow House-Style Documentation:** Add standard file header comment blocks and document your public methods using Doxygen-style markup.

**Static Scope Only (ADR-16):** Modules MUST be declared at global or static scope, not stack-allocated in `setup()`. The ESP32 has no MMU — stack-allocated modules will silently corrupt memory or cause hard faults when the framework invokes them after `setup()` returns.

**Late registration panics the device:** Calling `app.registerModule()` after `app.begin()` has been called will trigger a **fatal panic**. The registration registry is compacted and locked during boot — late registration is unconditionally forbidden. All registrations must occur in `setup()` before `app.begin()` is invoked.

**Stack-allocating modules (no MMU on ESP32):** Declaring a module as a local variable inside `setup()` creates a dangling pointer. The ESP32 has no MMU to trap this — it will silently corrupt memory or hard-fault when the framework calls the module's `tick()`. Always declare modules at global or `static` scope.
**Exposing hardware code in native builds:** Failing to wrap `#include <Wire.h>` or hardware-dependent drivers in `#ifdef ESP_PLATFORM` will cause host test builds to fail to compile.
**Implicit memory leaks in `tick()`:** Doing `JsonObject obj = doc.to<JsonObject>()` repeatedly inside `tick()` without clearing memory can lead to out-of-memory crashes.
**Duplicate registrations:** Calling `app.registerTickable(&myModule)` AND `app.registerModule(&myModule)` is redundant. The universal `registerModule()` call does all the work.
**Zero Framework Edits**: Adding or modifying board pinouts requires no changes to framework source files or internal headers.
**Single Source of Truth**: All hardware definitions (SPI/I2C pins, display type, board capabilities, pinout diagrams, allocation notes) reside in one self-contained header file per hardware variant.

**Build-Time Validation**: The framework contract validator (`board_contract.h`) verifies required symbols at compile-time and echoes the target board details to the compiler console without silent fallbacks.

**4.2 Historical Context: Why Manifest-First?**: Prior versions of the ESP32 App Foundation queried the GitHub REST API (`/repos/{repo}/releases`) directly from the device to discover updates (tracked in Issue #102). This approach was fundamentally flawed for embedded systems:

**Payload Size:** The GitHub releases API returns massive JSON payloads (often >100KB) containing verbose metadata for all release assets. The ESP32 cannot reliably buffer or stream-parse this without risking heap exhaustion or `JSON Parse Error: IncompleteInput` crashes.
**Rate Limiting:** Unauthenticated API calls from devices sharing a NAT IP were quickly rate-limited by GitHub (60 requests/hour), breaking update checks entirely.
**Pagination Complexity:** Finding the latest beta release often required paginating through multiple API responses on the device.

**`heap_caps_get_free_size()` ≠ allocatable memory.** Total free heap can report 60 KB, but if the largest contiguous block is only 20 KB, a 30 KB TLS allocation will still fail. Always check `heap_caps_get_largest_free_block()` for TLS readiness.

**No Heap Allocation in `tick()` Loops** — Code inside `tick()` executes dozens of times per second. `new`, `malloc`, `String` concatenation, and `std::vector::push_back()` inside `tick()` will fragment the heap within hours. Pre-allocate buffers as class members during `begin()`.

**Avoid Arduino `String`** — Arduino's `String` class uses hidden dynamic allocation and concatenation operations that fragment the heap quickly. Use `std::string`, `const char*`, or fixed-size `char` arrays. If `String` is unavoidable, call `reserve()` upfront.
**Pre-allocate Buffers** — For repeated I/O operations (serial parsing, HTTP responses), allocate the buffer once at initialisation and reuse it.

Even if total free heap is 60 KB, if fragmentation has reduced the largest contiguous block to 25 KB, the handshake will fail with an `mbedtls` allocation error. Use `heap_caps_get_largest_free_block(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL)` to check contiguous availability before initiating TLS connections.

**No Async Worker Pool**: There is no pool of 8 async workers (no 32 KB pool overhead).
**Single HTTP Task**: Exactly **one** httpd server task runs all HTTP handlers synchronously.

**SPI Flash Cache Rules During OTA** External PSRAM is inaccessible while the SPI flash cache is disabled during flash write operations. Any access to PSRAM during an OTA write causes a fatal CPU cache fault.

**HTTP Task Stack Must Remain Internal DRAM**: Never place the `httpd` task stack in PSRAM (`task_caps` must remain `MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL`), because direct-upload OTA (`Update.write`) and LittleFS config saves execute directly on the `httpd` task thread.
**OTA Worker Task Uses Internal DRAM**: `OTAUpdateManager` creates its persistent background worker task with `MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL` (`OTA_TASK_STACK_BYTES = 16384`).

**Mutual-Exclusion Gate**: `DisplayServiceHelper` checks `OTAUpdateManager::getState() != Idle` and returns HTTP 503 if an OTA update is active. For direct-upload OTA this is a hard guarantee (same httpd task); for scheduled background OTA the gate prevents overlap with manifest/download phases, making concurrent PSRAM access extremely unlikely.
If PSRAM is unavailable, `heap_caps_malloc(size, MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM)` returns `nullptr`. Always check the return value.

The primary threats are: **unauthorized access** from other devices on the same network, **firmware tampering** via OTA updates, and **credential theft** from flash storage.
The device is **not** a high-value target for state-level adversaries — the security model balances protection against practical attacks with the severe resource constraints of the ESP32.
The master key is a 256-bit AES key generated **once** on first boot via `esp_random()` and persists across firmware updates in NVS.
The master key is **not exportable** — it exists only in NVS on the physical device.
If NVS is erased, all encrypted credentials become **unrecoverable**. This is by design.
The `aesKey[32]` array is held in RAM for the lifetime of the process after `begin()` is called.

**TLS Handshake Peak:** ~40–50KB of contiguous heap.
**Concurrent Budget:** At most 2 concurrent TLS connections on a device with ~320KB SRAM.

**Acceptable:** When payload integrity is verified independently. The OTA pipeline uses `setInsecure()` for both manifest and firmware binary downloads because the firmware is cryptographically signed via `MbedTLSSignatureVerifier`. Transport security is redundant with payload verification.

**NOT acceptable:** When transmitting credentials or when the server's identity matters (e.g., `GithubClient` API calls that return release metadata — these use `setCACert()` with the pinned GitHub root CA).
Generated as 16 bytes of `esp_random()` (or `std::random_device` on native builds).
Delivered to the client as a cookie: `esp32_session=<32 hex chars>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`.
Validated via constant-time comparison (`_safeMemcmp()`) on every protected request.
A session is active when `_sessionToken` is not all-zero. Logging out clears it to all-zero.
**Auth disabled:** Returns `true` unconditionally — open access.
**Auth enabled:** Validates the session cookie first (browser-based MCP access), then falls back to `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header validation (constant-time comparison).
**Serial/USB transport:** MCP requests via serial are intentionally NOT guarded — physical serial access is treated as trusted.
**Storage:** DER-encoded at `/etc/server.key` and `/etc/server.crt`
**Static buffers:** Certificate loaded into a 1024-byte static buffer, key into a 256-byte static buffer (avoids heap fragmentation)
**Concurrency:** Generation uses an `std::atomic<bool>` guard (`_certGenRunning`) to prevent concurrent generation
**Token type:** Fine-grained Personal Access Token (not classic).
**Repository access:** Scoped to a **single** repository only.
**Permissions:** `Contents: Read-only` — no write, no account-level access.
**Expiration:** No expiration. Deployed devices may be offline for months; an expired PAT permanently bricks OTA capability.
`SECURITY_VERSION` is a compile-time macro injected by the build system.

On boot, `OTAUpdateManager::markAppValid()` calls `checkSecurityVersion()`, which compares the compiled `SECURITY_VERSION` against the value stored in NVS under the `"ota_security"` namespace, key `"sec_ver"`.
If the compiled version is **higher** than the stored version, NVS is updated to the new value.
If the compiled version is **lower**, the stored value is NOT decreased — the counter is monotonically increasing.
**Signature field collection** — The `.sig` bytes from the multipart upload are buffered into a 512-byte buffer.
**Verifier initialisation** — On the first firmware chunk, a `MbedTLSSignatureVerifier` is heap-allocated and initialized with the public key from `FrameworkConfig`.
**Binary magic validation** — The first byte must be `0xE9` (ESP32 binary header magic). Invalid headers are rejected immediately with a 400 response.
**Streaming hash** — Each firmware chunk is fed to `update()` for SHA-256 accumulation while simultaneously being written to the flash partition via `Update.write()`.
**Final verification** — On the last chunk, `verify()` is called with the collected signature bytes. If verification fails, the update is aborted.
**Why acceptable:** The downloaded firmware is cryptographically signed. `MbedTLSSignatureVerifier` provides payload integrity independent of transport security.
**Why not CA-pinned:** CA certificates expire, and the device may operate for years without firmware updates. A pinned cert that expires would permanently brick OTA capability.

Devices in the field verify OTA downloads using the **old public key** embedded in their running firmware.
A binary signed with the **new private key** will be rejected by those devices.
Therefore you must use the **old private key** to sign one final transitional release that ships the **new public key** embedded in firmware — only then can you switch to signing with the new key.

Step-by-step rotation procedure: `rm private_key.pem public_key.pem # remove old keys` (`xxd -i public_key.pem > include/publicKey.hpp`) (`git tag v1.2.4-transition # or whatever your next version is`) (`python3 scripts/deploy_release.py \`)

Any device that misses the transitional release will still carry the old public key and will be unable to accept OTA updates signed with the new private key. Those devices must be **manually re-flashed via USB**. Ensure maximum fleet adoption of the transitional release before discarding the old private key.
Keep a secure backup of the **old** private key until you are confident all deployed devices have received the transitional update. After that, the old key can be permanently deleted.

Tier 1 — Dev (`-dev.N`): `git tag v0.1.4-dev.1 && git push origin v0.1.4-dev.1`
`PATCH` should be the *next* unreleased patch number (i.e. current stable patch + 1).
`PRE_NUM` starts at 1 and increments with each functionally-distinct build.
Dev tags ARE published as GitHub pre-releases via `deploy_release.py` so that devices on the `dev` OTA channel can receive in-flight builds.
Agents MAY run `deploy_release.py` for `dev` tags autonomously (same autonomy as tag creation). Beta/stable deploys still require user approval.
Tier 2 — Beta (`-beta.N`): `git tag v0.1.4-beta.1 && git push origin v0.1.4-beta.1`
Beta tags replace all `dev` tags for that patch — once a beta is cut, subsequent in-flight work targets the **next** patch's `dev` series.

Beta builds are published as GitHub pre-releases via `deploy_release.py` **after hardware validation**. Tagging a beta does not automatically deploy it — build, flash, and validate on hardware first, then deploy when satisfied.
`scripts/deploy_release.py` will mark these as `--prerelease` automatically.
Tier 3 — Stable (no suffix): `git tag v0.1.4 && git push origin v0.1.4`
Stable tags must point at HEAD at build time (`deploy_release.py` verifies this).
Build, flash, and validate on hardware **before** deploying.
Stable GitHub Releases are NOT marked as pre-release.
A new stable tag supersedes all beta and dev tags for that patch.

**Tag before build** — when deploying a release, `deploy_release.py` auto-discovers the SemVer tag on HEAD via `discover_tag_on_head()`. The tag must exist before the build step so `inject_version.py` picks up the correct version.
**One canonical version per build** — if multiple SemVer tags exist on HEAD, `inject_version.py` selects the highest. Agents should avoid creating ambiguous double-tags on the same commit.

**Retag after housekeeping commits** — if non-firmware commits (agent workspace files, distillery artefacts, doc fixes) land after a release tag, `inject_version.py` will emit a WARNING. Before the next release, the tag must be moved to HEAD: (`git tag <tag> -f && git push origin --force <tag>`)

**Don't use non-SemVer branch tags for version tracking** — tags like `pr-18/wo3-display-tab` are branch markers, not version tags, and are ignored by `inject_version.py`. Do not create these with a `v` prefix.
